issues.t: Fuel injector "spider" assembly problems
issues.sym: Slow starts, rough idle, misfires, or a fuel smell.
issues.why: The central injector unit's nozzles can gum up or leak as the truck ages.
issues.next: Have a shop test it. Treat any fuel smell as urgent.

issues.t: Four-speed automatic slipping
issues.sym: Engine revs climb without acceleration, a gear goes missing, or reverse fails.
issues.why: The 4L60-E's 3-4 clutch pack is a known weak spot, especially in heavy SUVs that tow.
issues.next: Get a fluid check and road test soon. Stop towing until it is diagnosed.

issues.t: Dashboard pad cracking
issues.sym: Cracks appear across the top of the dash.
issues.why: Sun and heat break down the dash surface over time.
issues.next: Cosmetic. A dash cover helps. Keep cracks away from the air bag area in mind.

issues.t: Excess oil consumption
issues.sym: Frequent oil top-offs, low-oil message, blue smoke on startup, misfires.
issues.why: Oil passes the piston rings and burns, a problem tied to this engine family and its cylinder deactivation.
issues.next: Watch the dipstick closely and ask a GMC dealer for an oil consumption test.

issues.t: Lifter failure on V8s with cylinder deactivation
issues.sym: Tapping noise, misfire codes, shaking at idle, or power loss.
issues.why: The deactivating lifters can stick or collapse, sometimes ruining the camshaft.
issues.next: Diagnose quickly to limit engine damage.

issues.t: Brake assist loss recall
issues.sym: The brake pedal feels hard and the SUV takes longer to stop. A brake warning may appear.
issues.why: The engine-driven vacuum pump that powers the brake booster can lose output. GM recalled affected V8 models.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and have the fix done. A hard pedal deserves immediate attention.

issues.t: 6.2L engine recall for rod and crank defects
issues.sym: Engine knock, low oil pressure, rough running, or a sudden stall.
issues.why: Some engines had defective crankshaft or connecting rod parts that can fail.
issues.next: Check for open recalls. Stop driving if you hear knocking.

issues.t: Heated windshield washer module can short and catch fire (recall)
issues.sym: On trucks built with the heated washer fluid option, you may notice a burning smell or smoke from under the hood, or other electrical features acting up. Many owners never see a warning before the module overheats.
issues.why: The small heater that warms the washer fluid can short-circuit internally and overheat. GM recalled it twice and ended up disabling and removing the heater altogether.
issues.next: Run the VIN through the NHTSA recall lookup right away. If the recall is still open, book the free dealer repair now and park outside until it is done. Stop driving and have it towed if you smell burning or see smoke.

issues.t: A/C stops cooling from a cracked condenser
issues.sym: The air conditioning slowly gets weaker and then blows warm, often within the first few years. A shop may find the refrigerant charge is low or empty with no obvious damage.
issues.why: The A/C condenser at the front of the truck, which is built together with a transmission cooler, can crack from repeated heating and cooling and let the refrigerant escape. GM extended coverage on this part for a limited time on certain trucks.
issues.next: Have a shop check the system with leak dye or a sniffer before paying for a simple recharge, since a recharge alone will leak out again. Ask a GMC dealer whether special coverage 17336 ever applied to your VIN.

issues.t: Eight-speed automatic shudder at steady speed
issues.sym: A vibration that feels like driving over rumble strips, usually under light throttle at steady road speeds. It can come and go and may be joined by harsh or clunky shifts.
issues.why: The original transmission fluid in the eight-speed automatic used with the 6.2L engine in these years can take on moisture, which makes the torque converter clutch grab and release unevenly. GM issued a bulletin calling for a full exchange to a revised fluid.
issues.next: Ask a dealer or transmission shop about the fluid exchange in GM bulletin 18-NA-355. Get it done soon, because long-term shudder can wear out the torque converter.

issues.t: Magnetic Ride Control shocks leak or knock
issues.sym: On trucks with the Magnetic Ride Control suspension (standard on Denali), you may see oily fluid on a shock body, hear knocking over bumps, or notice a bouncier ride or a suspension service message.
issues.why: The electronically controlled shocks can develop seal leaks or internal noise as they age. GM has a service bulletin telling dealers how to judge a leak and to replace only the shock that has failed.
issues.next: Have the shocks looked at during your next service. A light film is normal, but fluid running down the shock or a clear change in ride means that shock should be replaced.

issues.t: Ten-speed transmission valve can lock the rear wheels (recall)
issues.sym: A sudden harsh downshift or a brief lockup of the rear wheels while driving, sometimes after a warning message about the transmission. Some owners first notice a rough shift into a lower gear.
issues.why: A control valve inside the ten-speed automatic can wear and lose pressure, which can cause an abrupt downshift that momentarily locks the rear wheels. The 2021 recall covers trucks with the 3.0L diesel, and a later recall covers 2022 trucks. Dealers load software that watches for the fault and limits the transmission before it can lock up.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and get the free software update done promptly. If you feel a harsh downshift or the rear wheels grab, slow down, pull over safely and have the truck towed to a dealer.

issues.t: Accelerator cable can snag and hold the throttle open (recall)
issues.sym: The pedal feels sticky, or it does not spring all the way back when you lift your foot.
issues.why: On these trucks the throttle cable could rub where it passes the dash and floor covering, so the throttle may not close fully.
issues.next: Treat a sticking pedal as an emergency: stop driving and have the cable routing inspected. Run the VIN through the NHTSA lookup for the free repair.

issues.t: Wipers can stop from cracked circuit board solder joints (recall)
issues.sym: Wipers quit altogether, stick on one speed, or sweep only now and then.
issues.why: Solder joints on the wiper control board crack after years of heat cycles and vibration, breaking the circuit.
issues.next: Have it fixed before you have to drive in rain or snow, and check the VIN for the open recall.

issues.t: Front brake rotor can crack (recall)
issues.sym: Grinding or knocking from a front wheel, a pedal that pulses, or a wheel that feels loose.
issues.why: A batch of front rotors was built out of specification and can crack in service; in the worst case the wheel can come away.
issues.next: Stop driving it and have the front brakes inspected now. The recall repair is free, so check the VIN first.

issues.t: Steering shaft pinch bolt can loosen and fall out (recall)
issues.sym: Vague or sloppy steering, a clunk when you turn, or in the worst case no steering response at all.
issues.why: The bolt that clamps the steering shaft coupling was not always tightened properly and can work its way out.
issues.next: Do not drive it until the coupling has been checked. Run the VIN for the free recall repair.

issues.t: Front passenger belt falls short of a federal restraint standard (recall)
issues.sym: Nothing you can feel day to day; the belt looks and works normally.
issues.why: The passenger restraint as built did not meet the federal requirement for how far the belt lets the head and neck travel in a crash.
issues.next: Check the VIN for the open recall and have the free correction done; keep using the belt in the meantime.

issues.t: ABS can grab on its own at low speed (recall)
issues.sym: At walking pace the pedal drops away, the brakes pulse, or the truck takes much longer to stop than you expect.
issues.why: Corrosion from road salt reaches the wheel speed sensor circuit, and the ABS reads it as a locked wheel and releases pressure it should be holding.
issues.next: Have the brakes and sensors checked right away, especially if you live where roads are salted. Check the VIN for the recall.

issues.t: Missing body plugs can let exhaust fumes into the cabin (recall)
issues.sym: An exhaust smell inside, worst with the tailgate or a window open, sometimes with headaches or drowsiness on longer drives.
issues.why: Plugs were left out of the wheelhouse panels, leaving a path for exhaust gas to reach the interior.
issues.next: Drive with the windows open and get it inspected immediately; exhaust in the cabin can make you pass out. The recall repair is free.

issues.t: Brake pipe can rub the body and leak fluid (recall)
issues.sym: A long or sinking pedal, a brake warning light, or wet spots under the truck.
issues.why: A brake pipe can touch the body where it was routed, and the rubbing wears through the line.
issues.next: Stop driving if the pedal has changed at all and have it towed in. Check the VIN for the free recall repair.

issues.t: Head restraint gap can pinch fingers (recall)
issues.sym: A gap in the seat head restraint where fingers can be caught while adjusting it.
issues.why: The head restraint design leaves a pinch point between moving parts.
issues.next: Keep children's hands clear while adjusting the seats and have the free recall correction done when convenient.

issues.t: Hydro-boost brake assist seal can split (recall)
issues.sym: The pedal suddenly needs much more effort, and the truck takes far longer to stop.
issues.why: A seal in the hydraulic brake booster relief valve can fracture, so the booster stops multiplying your pedal effort.
issues.next: Stop driving if the pedal has gone hard and have it towed. The recall fix is free, so check the VIN first.

issues.t: Rear center belt can ride up onto the stomach (recall)
issues.sym: The rear center lap belt sits high across the belly instead of low on the hips.
issues.why: The belt routing lets the lap portion slide up out of position, which can cause internal injuries in a crash.
issues.next: Have the free recall correction done and avoid seating a child in the rear center position until then.

issues.t: Rear door hinge welds may be out of specification (recall)
issues.sym: Nothing shows up in normal use; the door opens and closes as usual.
issues.why: Welds on a rear door hinge were not made to specification, which weakens the door in a side impact.
issues.next: Check the VIN and have the hinge inspected under the recall at no cost.

issues.t: Brake pedal pushrod retainer can be missing (recall)
issues.sym: The pedal may feel loose or disconnect from the brakes completely.
issues.why: A retainer that holds the pedal pushrod to the booster was left off during assembly, so the connection can separate.
issues.next: Do not drive it; have it towed and the pedal linkage checked under the free recall.

issues.t: Power steering hose can split at full lock (recall)
issues.sym: A groan or whine when turning, heavy steering, and red fluid under the front of the truck.
issues.why: Holding the wheel at full lock spikes pressure in a hose that was not strong enough, and it can fracture.
issues.next: Get it inspected right away: fluid on a hot engine can start a fire and the steering gets very heavy. The recall repair is free.

issues.t: Tire and loading label shows the wrong capacity (recall)
issues.sym: The sticker in the door jamb lists a load and tire figure that does not match the truck.
issues.why: The wrong label was applied at the factory, so owners may load the truck beyond what it is rated for.
issues.next: Ask the dealer for the corrected label under the recall and go by the owner's manual until then.

issues.t: Ignition lock can bind and snap back out of Run (recall)
issues.sym: The key is hard to turn, or the ignition jumps back from Run to Accessory and the engine dies.
issues.why: The ignition lock cylinder can bind so that the key does not stay where you put it, cutting engine, power steering and airbag power.
issues.next: Take everything heavy off the key ring and have it fixed under the recall right away; losing power steering at speed is dangerous.

issues.t: Contaminated control module can short and stall the truck (recall)
issues.sym: The engine cuts out while driving, warning lights come on together, or electrical features act strangely.
issues.why: Contamination inside a control module can create a short circuit that shuts the engine down without warning.
issues.next: Have the VIN checked and the module replaced under the recall before driving it far; a stall in traffic is a safety risk.

issues.t: Park lock can fail and let the truck roll (recall)
issues.sym: The truck creeps or rolls after you shift to Park and let go of the brake.
issues.why: The park mechanism may not engage fully, so nothing holds the driveline when the shifter says Park.
issues.next: Always set the parking brake, and have it repaired under the recall now; a rollaway can hurt someone.

issues.t: Wheel speed sensor fault can brake one wheel by itself (recall)
issues.sym: The truck pulls hard to one side under braking or tugs at the wheel on its own, usually with ABS or stability warnings.
issues.why: If a wheel speed sensor fails, the stability system can misread it and apply the brake at one wheel without the driver asking.
issues.next: Have the recall software update done as soon as you can and get any ABS warning diagnosed; this can cause a loss of control.

issues.t: Fuel pump assembly can leak from a missing regulator (recall)
issues.sym: A strong fuel smell, wet fuel around the tank area, or hard starting and stalling.
issues.why: Some fuel pump modules were built without a pressure regulator, so the system can run over pressure and leak.
issues.next: Park it outside, away from buildings, and have it towed for the free recall repair; leaking fuel is a fire risk.

issues.t: Daytime running lights can stay on with the headlights (recall)
issues.sym: The daytime running lights do not dim or switch off when you put the headlights on, and other drivers flash you.
issues.why: The lighting software does not turn the running lights off as the federal standard requires.
issues.next: Ask for the free software update at your next service visit.

issues.t: Third-row seat belt buckle rivet may be formed wrong (recall)
issues.sym: Nothing obvious; the buckle latches and releases normally.
issues.why: A rivet in the third-row buckle may not have been formed correctly, so the buckle may not hold in a crash.
issues.next: Have the buckle inspected under the recall at no cost and seat passengers elsewhere until then.

issues.t: Rear control arm bolts can break (recall)
issues.sym: Clunking or banging from the rear over bumps, a rear wheel that looks out of line, or wandering at speed.
issues.why: Outer rear control arm bolts can fracture, which lets the wheel move out of position.
issues.next: Stop driving and have it inspected under the recall; a broken link can cause a loss of control.

issues.t: No warning light if brake fluid runs low (recall)
issues.sym: The brake warning light never comes on, even when the reservoir is low.
issues.why: The instrument cluster software does not light the required warning for low brake fluid, so a slow leak can go unnoticed.
issues.next: Get the free software update and check the fluid level yourself in the meantime.

issues.t: Wrong diesel fuel tank can leak in a rollover (recall)
issues.sym: Nothing in normal driving; the tank only matters in a crash or rollover.
issues.why: Some diesel trucks were built with a fuel tank that does not meet the rollover leak requirement.
issues.next: Run the VIN and have the tank replaced under the recall at no cost.

issues.t: Wrong front hub bolts can loosen (recall)
issues.sym: Clicking or clunking from a front wheel, vibration that gets worse with speed, or a wheel that feels loose.
issues.why: Trucks built with certain large wheels got the wrong front hub bolts, which can stretch or work loose.
issues.next: Stop driving and have the front hubs inspected under the recall; a loose hub can cause a loss of control.

issues.t: Missing transfer case part can lock the wheels (do-not-drive recall)
issues.sym: Sudden grinding or binding from under the truck, or the wheels locking up with no warning.
issues.why: A component can be missing inside the transfer case, which lets it jam and lock the front or rear wheels.
issues.next: Do not drive it. Check the VIN and have it towed to the dealer for the free repair.

issues.t: Transfer case can lock the wheels without warning (do-not-drive recall)
issues.sym: Grinding or binding from the driveline, or wheels that suddenly stop turning freely.
issues.why: On certain four-wheel-drive and all-wheel-drive trucks a part can be missing from the transfer case, letting it seize.
issues.next: Do not drive it. Run the VIN and arrange a tow to the dealer for the free repair.

issues.t: Radio may be missing the electronic owner's manual (recall)
issues.sym: The owner information pages in the radio menu are blank or missing.
issues.why: The radio did not download the electronic owner's manual, which carries required safety information.
issues.next: Ask the dealer to load the manual at no charge, or use the printed or online version in the meantime.

issues.t: Intake manifold gaskets leak coolant on the 5.7L V8
issues.sym: Coolant level keeps dropping with no puddle, crusty residue on top of the engine, a sweet smell through the vents, or oil that looks like coffee with milk.
issues.why: The intake gaskets used on this Vortec V8 soften and let coolant escape, sometimes outward and sometimes down into the oil.
issues.next: Have the cooling system pressure-tested soon. If the oil looks milky, stop driving it until the gaskets are replaced, or the bearings will suffer.
